subject: Elements inside a "display:none" tag do not get initialized by render* functions

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Elements inside a "display:none" tag do not get initialized by render* functions
parts:
Hi,

I've noticed that if I have a dynamic (uiOutput) element that is initially hidden when the app starts by being inside an element with "display:none", it won't be rendered in the server. 

Example:
library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    tags$head(tags$style(HTML(
      ".foo { display: none; }"
    ))),
    div(uiOutput("bar"), class = "foo"),
    p("world")
  ),
 
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    output$bar <- renderUI({ tags$p("hello") })    
  }
)

If you look at the page HTML, you'll see that bar is 
<div id="bar" class="shiny-html-output shiny-bound-output"></div>
and shiny hasn't actually rendered the element. 

If you make the element invisible using `visibility: hidden`, it works fine, so it's really something about the fact that it's `display: none`.  But I don't want to use visibility:hidden because then the space of it is still taken up on the page.


Can someone confirm if this is by design (and if so, then why?) or a bug? I'd like to know if there's a workaround for this meanwhile. I have a lot of use cases where I like to start with something initially hidden and I don't always like to use conditionalPanel for this.

Thanks

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Elements inside a "display:none" tag do not get initialized by render* functions
parts:
(Hi Dean, when I found out about shinyjs yesterday I meant to reach out to you about exactly this issue, which I knew you would run into.)

It's a feature. The goal is to not spend cycles rendering something that won't be seen anyway. This is really helpful in apps that have a bunch of tabs, some of which contain expensive plots or whatever.

However, the feature is better than it looks--it's intended that when the element goes from display:none to display:block or whatever, then Shiny would realize it and start executing the render block that belongs to it. Unfortunately for performance reasons we don't want to just poll on these elements, so instead we need a little help from whomever is showing/hiding the element. If you raise a jQuery "shown"/"hidden" event then Shiny will know to go look for newly displayed or hidden outputs. You can see how conditionalPanel does it here.

You can turn off this behavior on a per-output basis using outputOptions(output, id, suspendWhenHidden=FALSE).
